memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Choose some wise, understanding and respected men from each of your tribes, and I will set them over you. You answered me, "What you propose to do is good." So I took the leading men of your tribes, wise and respected men, and appointed them to have authority over you—as commanders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties and of tens and as tribal officials. - Deut 1:13-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses recalls how leaders were chosen to help him: "wise, understanding and respected men from each of your tribes." The qualities God's people looked for were not wealth, popularity, or raw ambition, but wisdom, understanding, and a good reputation. These were the marks of those fit to lead and serve God's people. Character mattered more than charisma.

This is a helpful reminder in a world that often elevates leaders for the wrong reasons — for being impressive, forceful, or well-connected, rather than wise and trustworthy. God's pattern is different. The people He honours with responsibility are those marked by godly character: wisdom to discern, understanding to judge fairly, and a life respected by others.

The New Testament carries this same emphasis. When leaders were chosen in the early church, they looked for people full of the Spirit and wisdom, of good reputation and proven character (Acts 6:3; 1 Tim 3:1-7). God cares deeply about the character of those who lead and serve His people. Gifts and abilities matter, but character is the foundation.

There is a challenge here for each of us, whether we lead or not. God is at work forming these qualities in all His people — wisdom, understanding, integrity. We should desire to grow in godly character, not merely in skills or status. And when we choose those to follow or entrust with responsibility, we do well to look for the qualities God values. Above all, we follow the perfect Leader, Christ, in whom all wisdom and understanding dwell (Col 2:3), and who is shaping us into His likeness.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you value godly character over charisma in yourself and in leaders?
2. What qualities is God calling you to grow in — wisdom, understanding, integrity?
3. How does following Christ, the perfect Leader, shape the way you lead or serve?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to value godly character above impressive appearances. Grow in me wisdom, understanding, and integrity, and help me to follow Christ, in whom all wisdom dwells, as He shapes me into His likeness. Amen.
